Exploratory Data Analysis: Olist E‑Commerce Dataset¶

Name: Dhakshitha Mohan Rao
ID: GH1044699
Dataset: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce

Objective¶

The goal of this analysis is to explore customer behavior, seller performance, product trends, delivery efficiency, and payment patterns within the Olist marketplace.
Through a series of visualizations, we aim to uncover actionable business insights that can support decision‑making in marketing, logistics, inventory planning, and customer satisfaction improvement.

Audience¶

This analysis is intended for:

  • E‑commerce business strategists
  • Operations & logistics managers
  • Marketing teams
  • Data analysts and product managers
  • Stakeholders interested in customer experience and marketplace optimization

Dataset Overview¶

The Olist dataset contains multiple interconnected tables covering:

  • Customer demographics
  • Order timelines
  • Product attributes
  • Seller information
  • Payments
  • Reviews
  • Delivery performance

These datasets collectively allow a full‑cycle analysis of the customer journey from purchase to delivery and feedback.

Dataset Overview¶

The Olist Brazilian E-Commerce dataset is a multi-table relational dataset that represents the full lifecycle of an online order — from customer placement to delivery and review.

It allows end-to-end analysis of marketplace operations including customers, sellers, logistics, payments, products, and satisfaction.

Main Tables¶

  • Customers: Location and identity
  • Orders: Purchase and delivery timestamps
  • Order Items: Product-level purchase details
  • Products: Category and physical attributes
  • Payments: Payment methods and values
  • Reviews: Customer ratings and comments
  • Sellers: Seller location and identity

Feature Engineering¶

Derived metrics created:

  • delivery_time_days: Actual delivery duration
  • approval_time_hours: Time from purchase to approval
  • delivery_delay_days: Difference between estimated and actual delivery
  • order_month: Monthly grouping for trend analysis

Data Quality Assessment¶

  • Missing timestamps in orders and product attributes
  • Many reviews lack written comments
  • No duplicate rows across datasets
    Despite missing fields, core transactional data is complete and suitable for analysis.
In [7]:
orders['delivery_time_days'] = (
    orders['order_delivered_customer_date'] -
    orders['order_purchase_timestamp']
).dt.days

orders['approval_time_hours'] = (
    orders['order_approved_at'] -
    orders['order_purchase_timestamp']
).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

orders['delivery_delay_days'] = (
    orders['order_delivered_customer_date'] -
    orders['order_estimated_delivery_date']
).dt.days
In [8]:
df = orders.merge(customers, on="customer_id", how="left") \
           .merge(order_items, on="order_id", how="left") \
           .merge(products, on="product_id", how="left") \
           .merge(translation, on="product_category_name", how="left") \
           .merge(payments, on="order_id", how="left") \
           .merge(reviews, on="order_id", how="left")

print("Final dataset shape:", df.shape)

Final dataset shape: (119143, 40)

EDA Overview¶

The analysis focuses on:

  1. Revenue & Product Performance
  2. Customer Behavior
  3. Delivery & Logistics Performance
  4. Customer Satisfaction

Goal: Connect operational performance with customer experience and business outcomes.

Monthly Sales Trend¶

Analyze monthly revenue patterns to detect seasonality, peak periods, and demand fluctuations for better forecasting and planning.

In [12]:
df['order_month'] = df['order_purchase_timestamp'].dt.to_period('M')

monthly_sales = (
    df.groupby('order_month')['price']
      .sum()
      .reset_index()
)

monthly_sales['order_month'] = monthly_sales['order_month'].astype(str)


# FIGURE LAYOUT

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16,7))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(1,5)


# LEFT : LINE CHART

ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0,:4])

sns.lineplot(
    data=monthly_sales,
    x='order_month',
    y='price',
    marker='o',
    linewidth=3,
    color="#1F77B4",
    ax=ax
)

# Highlight maximum month
max_row = monthly_sales.loc[monthly_sales['price'].idxmax()]

ax.scatter(
    max_row['order_month'],
    max_row['price'],
    color="red",
    s=120,
    zorder=5
)

ax.annotate(
    "Highest Sales",
    (max_row['order_month'], max_row['price']),
    xytext=(0,20),
    textcoords="offset points",
    ha='center',
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight='bold',
    color='red'
)

ax.set_title(
    "Monthly Sales Revenue Trend",
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=15
)

ax.set_xlabel("Month", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Revenue (R$)", fontsize=12)

plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45)

sns.despine()

Delivery Performance & Satisfaction¶

Compare delivery times across review scores to understand how logistics speed influences customer ratings and overall satisfaction.

In [14]:
delivery_reviews = df[['delivery_time_days', 'review_score']].dropna()

# Remove unrealistic delivery times (optional but improves readability)
delivery_reviews = delivery_reviews[
    (delivery_reviews['delivery_time_days'] >= 0) &
    (delivery_reviews['delivery_time_days'] <= 60)
]

Payment Behavior¶

Explore the distribution of payment methods to identify dominant transaction types and optimize checkout experience.

In [15]:
payment_counts = df['payment_type'].value_counts()
payment_percent = (payment_counts / payment_counts.sum() * 100).sort_values()

categories = payment_percent.index
values = payment_percent.values

# Angles
angles = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, len(categories), endpoint=False)


# FIGURE

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16,7))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(1,5)


# LEFT : RADIAL BAR CHART

ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0,:4], polar=True)

colors = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0.3, 0.9, len(values)))

bars = ax.bar(
    angles,
    values,
    width=0.7,
    color=colors,
    edgecolor="white",
    linewidth=2
)

# Category labels
ax.set_xticks(angles)
ax.set_xticklabels(categories, fontsize=11)

# FIX: Move labels outward to avoid collision
for angle, value in zip(angles, values):
    ax.text(
        angle,
        value + 6,   # Increased spacing for clarity
        f"{value:.1f}%",
        ha='center',
        va='center',
        fontsize=11,
        fontweight='bold'
    )

ax.set_title(
    "Payment Method Share (Radial Bar Chart)",
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight="bold",
    pad=25
)

ax.set_yticklabels([])
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

Visualize where customers are concentrated across Brazil to identify major urban hubs, regional demand patterns, and areas with strong or emerging market presence.

city_counts = df['customer_city'].value_counts().head(10)
cities = city_counts.index
values = city_counts.values

Customer Revenue Concentration (Pareto Analysis)¶

Impact of Delivery Delays on Order Outcomes¶

Visualize how early, on‑time, and late deliveries relate to order completion or cancellation to understand how delivery reliability affects business outcomes.

In [21]:
delay_df = df[['delivery_delay_days', 'order_status']].dropna()

# Categorize delay
def classify_delay(x):
    if x < 0:
        return "Early Delivery"
    elif x <= 0:
        return "On Time"
    else:
        return "Late Delivery"

delay_df['delay_category'] = delay_df['delivery_delay_days'].apply(classify_delay)

# Cross-tab
ct = pd.crosstab(delay_df['order_status'], delay_df['delay_category'])

# Normalize for proportion view
ct_norm = ct.div(ct.sum(axis=1), axis=0)


# FIGURE

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16,7))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(1,5)


# LEFT: STACKED BAR

ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0,:4])

ct_norm.plot(
    kind='bar',
    stacked=True,
    colormap='viridis',
    ax=ax
)

ax.set_title(
    "Impact of Delivery Delay on Order Status",
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight="bold"
)

ax.set_xlabel("Order Status")
ax.set_ylabel("Proportion of Orders")

plt.xticks(rotation=45)

Conclusion¶

The exploratory analysis of the Olist Brazilian E‑Commerce dataset reveals clear patterns across revenue, logistics, customer behavior, and satisfaction:

  • Revenue is concentrated in a small set of product categories, especially health_beauty and watches_gifts.
  • Monthly sales show strong seasonality, with notable peaks in late 2017.
  • Delivery time and delivery delays significantly influence customer satisfaction.
  • Credit cards dominate payment behavior, followed by boleto.
  • Review scores are polarized, with many 5‑star and 1‑star ratings.
  • Logistics performance is a stronger driver of satisfaction than product price or payment value.

These insights highlight the operational and strategic levers that shape marketplace performance.

Business Recommendations¶

  • Improve logistics reliability to reduce delivery delays and increase customer satisfaction.
  • Prioritize top‑revenue categories with targeted marketing and inventory optimization.
  • Monitor seller performance and enforce stricter SLAs for consistently delayed deliveries.
  • Enhance customer communication during shipping to reduce uncertainty and negative reviews.
  • Optimize checkout flow for credit card users while maintaining alternative payment options.
  • Develop customer loyalty programs for high‑value repeat buyers.

Limitations¶

  • Missing timestamps in delivery fields (e.g., 2965 missing delivered_customer_date) reduce accuracy in delay calculations.
  • Product category information is incomplete (610 missing category names).
  • Review comments are largely missing (58k+ missing messages), limiting sentiment analysis.
  • No cost, profit, or inventory data is available, restricting financial modeling.
  • Dataset represents historical marketplace behavior and may not reflect current trends.

Future Work¶

  • Build predictive models for delivery delays and customer satisfaction.
  • Perform customer segmentation using RFM or clustering techniques.
  • Conduct sentiment analysis on review comments (after cleaning missing data).
  • Forecast monthly sales using time‑series models.
  • Analyze seller clusters based on delivery performance and product mix.
  • Develop a recommendation system using product and customer behavior data.
